subject: Renewal: term swap + burst uplift — redline handoff and sign path
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Morrison <elise.morrison@silverline.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: term swap + burst uplift (draft redlines attached)

Hi Elise —

Thanks for the call last week. Attached is a single-package renewal draft that reflects the two things Silverline asked for: (1) move from a 24→36 month term (effective 2027-06-01) and (2) a temporary burst uplift for Q3 to handle your marketing seasonal spike.

What I attached:
- Silverline_Renewal_Draft_MSA_2027-03-29.pdf (redline of MSA)
- OrderForm_Redline_2027-03-29.docx (order form with quantities/pricing)
- Silverline_Capacity_Plan_2027-03-29.xlsx (proposed ramp schedule)

As a reminder, the key commercial points are:
- Term: start 2027-06-01, 36 months, annual invoicing (prorated first invoice)
- Capacity baseline: 250k LLM tokens/day (committed) with a burst to 650k tokens/day for 90 days (Q3 window)
- Pricing: baseline rate unchanged; burst billed at blended uplift 1.6x baseline unit rate

Asks:
1) Kim/legal — quick read on the MSA redline, I highlighted two new clauses (proration and temporary surge carve). Can you confirm we can accept Silverline's requested language or propose minimal edits?
2) Monica/CS — can you confirm the ramp in the Capacity_Plan and whether engineering needs any additional lead time?
3) Elise/Derek — once legal signs off, we'll send a combined DocuSign packet. Any internal procurement timing constraints?

Proposed next step: legal signoff by 4/1 so we can get procurement signature and DocuSign out the week of 4/4.

Thanks —
Ben

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: term swap + burst uplift (draft redlines attached)

Ben — thanks for the packet and for consolidating. Quick notes from procurement/legal at our side (Derek looping in):

- We reviewed the MSA redline and added a counter-markup on the proration language — mainly concerned about billing alignment for the partial first period. I attached our counter redline: Silverline_Counter_Redline_2027-03-30.docx.
- Procurement question: can the burst be structured with a single invoice capture (i.e., charge actual burst usage monthly rather than a one-time prepayment)? That avoids our monthly cashflow headaches.
- On term length: we are comfortable with 36 months but want an SLA uplift tied to the higher commit (uptime/latency SLOs for production model).

High-level ask: can Redwood accomodate monthly actuals billing for burst and a measurable performance uplift tied to the new commit level? If so, we should be able to sign quickly.

On timing, procurement needs to review the DocuSign bundle and will try to turn in 3–5 business days after we get the final MSA and order form.

Thanks —
Elise

Thanks, Ben / Elise — looping in product/eng notes so everyone is aligned.

Operational read: the burst request (650k tokens/day for 90 days) is feasible but we need a lead time window for capacity pre-warm:
- Action: Redwood infra needs 10 business days after DocuSign to schedule a dedicated pool and run smoke-testing before the first burst day.
- Suggested cadence: 2027-06-01 term start, baseline active; pre-warm for burst begins 2027-08-10 so burst window 2027-08-20 → 2027-11-17 (90 days).

On the billing suggestion from procurement: we can bill burst monthly based on actuals. Monica confirms this is fine commercially; we'll attach an invoice example to the order form.

Kim — can you confirm whether the counter redline on proration is acceptable or needs alternative language? Also we should add the SLO appendix referencing the higher commit (simple uplift to 99.95% region-level uptime and latency p90 target of 200ms for inference).

I'll update the Capacity_Plan spreadsheet and re-upload if legal and procurement agree.

Monica

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: term swap + burst uplift (draft redlines attached)

Hi all — legal review attached (MSA_final_redline_2027-04-01.pdf). Summary of our position:

1) Proration language — APPROVE with edit: replace your proposed paragraph with the attached clean clause that clarifies first invoice proration methodology (days-of-service calculation) and includes a 30-day invoice dispute window.
2) Burst billing — APPROVE monthly actuals billing, but we need to preserve a cap: if cumulative burst usage exceeds 2x expected burst forecast during the 90-day window we reserve the right to bill at 1.8x blended rate for the overage period. Clause included in order form redline.
3) SLA appendix — we can include the uplifted SLOs. Legal requests we: (a) limit the latency p90 obligation to requests routed to the dedicated pool only, and (b) include a force-majeure carveout for third-party infra incidents.

If Silverline agrees to the short edits in the attached PDF we can finalize and send a DocuSign bundle. I added minor markup to the OrderForm and MSA.

Next step: Ben — please confirm you want the DocuSign bundle with the attached final redlines. I'll approve the final packet for signature on receipt.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park | Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
